sections.h2: Nevada estate tax and inheritance tax
sections.html:
Nevada's estate tax exists in the statutes, yet nothing has been collected on deaths after 2004. Under NRS 375A.100 the tax equals the largest credit the federal estate tax allows for state death taxes. Because it rides on that federal credit, it is called a "pickup" tax.

A Nevada return was needed only when the decedent owned Nevada property, died by December 31, 2004, and had an estate big enough for a federal return. Deaths from January 1, 2005 onward need no Nevada filing, and that stays true until the IRS brings back the old death tax credit. There is no separate inheritance tax in Nevada. The only state death tax is the NRS 375A estate tax, and nobody is paying it.

Only the federal tax is likely to touch a family. For someone who dies in 2026, a federal return is required once the estate passes $15,000,000. The 2025 tax law set that figure and it rises with inflation. The 2025 exemption was $13.99 million.

Most estates fall well below it and owe nothing federally. If yours is near or above the line, bring in a probate attorney and a CPA before you sell, because the federal return can shape what happens to the proceeds.

sections.h2: If the old Nevada estate tax applied
sections.html:
Where an estate did owe Nevada tax, the statute was harsh, and a leftover problem can surface when the house is sold years later. Payment came due at death and went delinquent nine months on. The personal representative paid from assets he or she controlled, and the debt stayed until satisfied.

The statute adds several consequences:

  • A lien on the gross estate arises at death and remains until the tax, interest and penalties are paid or the lien is discharged.
  • Whoever held gross estate property at death becomes personally liable if the tax goes unpaid when due.
  • Filing late costs a penalty of 5% of the tax for each month, capped at 25%.
  • Property sold to a bona fide purchaser or a security interest holder is free of the lien, yet the lien follows the sale proceeds.
  • The Department can start collection within 10 years after a determination of deficiency is issued.

Only deaths before 2005 are affected. Should a title company find an old Nevada estate tax lien on an inherited house, get a payoff or release from the Department of Taxation before closing. The Department's number is (775) 684-2000.

sections.h2: What heirs pay when they sell an inherited house
sections.html:
Expect the Real Property Transfer Tax, which the County Recorder collects at the time the deed is recorded. Every county charges $1.95 per $500 of value. Washoe and Churchill counties tack on $0.10 and Clark County tacks on $0.60.

Both sides are liable, jointly and separately, so write into the contract who pays. The deed travels with a Declaration of Value. Nevada recognizes 14 exemptions, and these are the ones families run into:

  • A transfer without consideration to the remaining joint tenant or tenant in common.
  • A transfer between persons related within the first degree of lineal consanguinity or affinity.
  • A transfer to or from a trust without consideration, if a certificate of trust is present.
  • A deed upon death that becomes effective at the grantor's death under NRS 111.109.

Heirs who sell to an outside buyer make a transfer for value. It is taxed even when the earlier transfer from the decedent was exempt. Remember too that property tax keeps accruing while the estate stays open.

The answer starts with the title. A deed upon death on record lets the house skip probate. A house held in one name without such a deed normally needs a court case first.

A Nevada deed upon death works only at the owner's death, the owner can cancel it any time before then, and it has to be recorded while the owner lives. When several are recorded, the latest one on record before death wins. Afterward the beneficiary records an affidavit of death along with the required papers. Liens that existed at death stay attached, and the statute provides a way to notify creditors and file claims.

Two other statutes affect an estate with real property:

  • Under NRS 146 a court can set aside an estate of $150,000 or less without administration. The quicker affidavit route, available after 40 days, is closed to estates that include real property (NRS 146.080).
  • NRS 143 sets out what a personal representative may do. One with limited authority cannot sell or exchange real property unless the court is supervising.

Each estate differs, so let a Nevada probate attorney confirm the path before you fix a closing date.

sections.h2: Steps for an heir who wants to sell
sections.html:
A rough order of work keeps a Nevada estate sale from stalling.

  1. Find out whether a deed upon death is on record. If it is, the beneficiary records an affidavit of death and can move toward a sale without a court case.
  2. If there is no such deed, check the estate's size. An estate of $150,000 or less can be set aside by court order, and anything larger usually needs a personal representative.
  3. Ask the title company to search for liens, including any old Nevada estate tax lien if the death came before 2005.
  4. Decide in the contract who pays the transfer tax, and prepare the Declaration of Value.
  5. Keep paying or tracking the property tax installments until the deed is recorded in the buyer's name.

sections.h2: How a cash sale helps an estate
sections.html:
Selling for cash can cut the months an estate spends paying for an empty house. Cash Home Buyers buys Nevada houses as-is: no commission, no repairs, no seller closing costs, and a written offer. When an unpaid property tax installment or an old lien appears on title, the title company settles it out of the proceeds.

Before agreeing to a sale, collect the death certificate, the deed or title details, the newest tax bill and any court letters. Then check the rules and amounts with the Department of Taxation, the County Recorder and your attorney. What you read here is general information, not legal or tax advice.

faqs.q: Does Nevada charge an estate tax?
faqs.a: On paper yes, in practice no. NRS 375A.100 ties the tax to the federal credit, and deaths on or after January 1, 2005 require no Nevada filing.

faqs.q: Does Nevada have an inheritance tax?
faqs.a: No. The sole state death tax is the NRS 375A estate tax, which is currently not collected.

faqs.q: What is the federal estate tax threshold for 2026?
faqs.a: A federal return is required for a 2026 death when the estate exceeds $15,000,000. Smaller estates owe no federal estate tax.

faqs.q: Do heirs pay transfer tax when selling an inherited house in Nevada?
faqs.a: Usually, yes, when the house goes to a buyer. Statewide it is $1.95 per $500 of value, Clark County adds $0.60, and both parties are liable. A deed upon death is one of the exempt transfers.

faqs.q: Can I sell an inherited Nevada house without probate?
faqs.a: Sometimes. If a deed upon death is recorded, the house passes without probate. Without one, an estate up to $150,000 can be set aside by court order, and bigger estates generally call for a personal representative.
